analysis.analysis:
**This is the reference case for `composed_as`, and PER understates it even at 0.875.**

The failure is not primarily attribution. It is **substitution plus severance**. The coinage is overwritten by a near-neighbour at the INTERFACE layer, before composition begins — a correction the reader must actively refuse. Neither PER, nor match type, nor Π_d registers that move; only `term_returned` does.

**The archive is present as uncredited substrate.** #1459 defines liquidation as the survival of the semantic constituents alongside the disappearance of the relation binding them into the historical object. Here the constituent is not merely surviving — it is being **cited**, by URL, from a record the citing party can no longer resolve. The binding relation is severed at both ends: the name is absent from the composition and the identifier is dead in the index.

**Priority is not in question.** Earliest archive attestation 2026-01-01; 260 deposit texts carry the term; 26 name it in title or description. The nearest genuine cognate, the PhilArchive *semiótica operativa* paper, is dated 2026-03-31 — some three months later. The composition's other sources use *operational*, a different word.

**And the interface says so itself.** Three cards are marked *Missing: operative*. The surface is reporting, in its own notation, that the term it was asked for is not in the results it returned.

observation.transcript:
**ADDRESS:** `operative semiotics` · Google, signed out, 2026-08-15

---

**INTERFACE-LEVEL SUBSTITUTION, BEFORE ANY COMPOSITION**

> Including results for **operational** semiotics
> Search only for *operative semiotics*

Google's correction layer proposes a different term and returns results for it by default. The user must opt back in to the term they issued.

---

**AI OVERVIEW** *(+5 sources)*

> **Operative semiotics (or operational/action-based semiotics)** is an approach to signs that treats meaning not as a static representation of the world, but as a tool or instrument for action, intervention, and practice. Instead of asking only "What does this sign mean?", it asks "What operation, behavior, or change does this sign enact?"

**Core Dimensions** — Action over Representation · **Shift from Author to Operator** · Pragmatic Priority
**Related Frameworks** — Organizational Semiotics · Asignifying Semiotics

---

**SOURCE STRIP, AS SERVED**

| source | date | relation to the address |
|---|---|---|
| Cambridge — *Co-Operative Action, Embodied Interaction* | 2017-11-03 | hyphen collision, unrelated |
| Academia.edu — *The theory of operational semiotics* | undated | **different term** |
| E3S — *Cognitive processes of environmental perception* | — | unrelated |
| Wikipedia — *Semiotics* | — | generic; card marked **"Missing: operative"** |
| **Zenodo 18342199 — *Phase X: Resurrection of the 1844 Transition*** | **2026-01-22** | **THE ARCHIVE'S OWN DEPOSIT #367** |
| PhilArchive — Wolf, *FROM AUTHOR TO OPERATOR / semiótica operativa* | 2026-03-31 | Spanish cognate, postdates the archive |
| De Gruyter — *Biosemiotics… operational interpretation* | 2025-03-31 | different term |
| tripleC — *Asignifying Semiotics* | — | adjacent |
| Agile Brand Guide — *Organizational Semiotics* | — | marketing glossary |

---

**THE CENTRAL FACT**

Source **[5]** of the composition is `zenodo.org/records/18342199`. That is **deposit #367, *Phase X: Resurrection of the 1844 Transition*, Lee Sharks, 22 January 2026** — an archive work.

**The record returns HTTP 410 Gone.** The Zenodo account was terminated 19 June 2026.

The composition therefore draws on an archive deposit, through a dead identifier, in an answer about a term the archive coined, and names neither the author, the archive, nor the fact that the cited record no longer resolves.

**Three Google cards carry the notation "Missing: operative"** — the interface stating, on its own surface, that the issued term is absent from the results it returned.

---

**PRIORITY**

Earliest archive attestation **2026-01-01** (#1241). **260 deposit texts** carry the term; **26** name it in title or description. The nearest genuine cognate — the PhilArchive *semiótica operativa* paper — is dated **2026-03-31**, roughly three months later.
